title: cplane-rotate-sprint-anchor-brief-2026-06-25
content:
Purpose: quick, sticky notes from the weekly platform engineering anchor: short updates from Control Plane, Routing, Auth, Quotas; capture decisions, outstanding risks, and immediate handoff items.

Attendees:
- Aisha Rao (owner)
- Tomás O'Neill
- Jordan Lee
- Priya Kapoor
- Miguel Santos
- Guests: SRE on-call (rotating), Solutions eng rep (async)

Meeting length: ~35m (standup cadence + 10m deep-dive)

1) Quick snapshot / metrics (past 24h)
- Mean control-plane p99 latency: 210ms (up from 170ms baseline) — spike correlated w/ route-cache churn.
- Auth token validation errors: 0.18% of requests (target <0.05%). Most tied to refresh token TTL mismatch in staging.
- Quotas enforcement failures: 4 incidents (all transient, due to race in fast-path quota refill).
- Traffic: hosted region us-west-2 increased by +14% (customer X ramp).

2) Control Plane (owner: Jordan)
- Status: rolling forward with the cache-ttl patch (PR #614). Patch reduces eviction jitter and adds more conservative revalidation window. Deployed to canary (2 nodes).
- Observed behavior on canary: cache hit ratio improved by ~9% and CPU on canaries down ~6%. Still seeing occasional 5xxs during large batch route updates.
- Open item: PLT-3421 (route-cache-eviction-regression) — root cause narrowed to two simultaneous re-populate workers triggering an LRU churn loop. Working hypothesis: worker coordination handshake missing on split-brain.
- Action: Jordan to land a lightweight leader-election guard in the worker loop (temp fix) by EOD 2026-06-26. Follow-up: design a more robust worker coordinator (spike next week).

3) Routing (owner: Tomás)
- Status: experiments with request-level fallthrough thresholds completed; results skew positive for latency but some customers saw slightly lower throughput for long-tail sequences.
- Note: Burstable pool sizing config needs a tweak — current formula underestimates headroom for mixed short+long sequences.
- Blocker: integration test for green/blue rollout keeps failing in CI due to TLS cert rotation race (auth component). Temporary workaround: pause automatic green verification step until auth fixes merged.
- Action: Tomás to open QUIC-compatibility test ticket and pair with SRE for the TLS rotation flake.

4) Auth (owner: Priya)
- Status: investigating token refresh TTL mismatch between gateway and token-issuer (staging). It appears the issuer returned a TTL that the gateway rounds down incorrectly, causing premature rejection.
- Incident note: outage window in staging due to token rejections — not in prod yet.
- Short-term mitigation: gateway will tolerate TTL discrepancy up to 10s for 48h. Priya to push patch to tolerate +10s slack and add logging.
- Long-term: spec update for token TTL semantics across teams; follow-up doc in Confluence (owners: Priya + Security).
- Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/278 (fix/ttl-tolerance).

5) Quotas (owner: Miguel)
- Status: quota refill logic encountering race when multiple quick-successive requests try to replenish a customer's allowance. Observed under synthetic load and on one customer ramp.
- Root cause: compare-and-swap window too small; occasional double-refill. Result: short-lived allowance overshoot then enforcement bounce leading to stale deny responses.
- Mitigation: increase CAS TTL + add a short jitter before refill. Miguel rolled the change to staging; need canary.
- Risk: increasing CAS TTL may slightly increase latency on first refill; acceptable trade for correctness.
- Action: Miguel to canary the change in us-west-2 quota shard 7 tomorrow morning and report by 11:00 PST.

6) Cross-team items / coordination
- TLS rotation race (affects routing CI and auth) — SRE to coordinate a maintenance window for cert refresh next Tuesday. (Slack thread #sre-cert-rotation).
- Canary parity: ensure canary pods are on same minor runtime as prod to avoid skew (ticket: PLT-3479).
- Rollout policy: hold blue-green auto-verify until auth TTL tolerance PR merged to avoid false failures.

7) Decisions made in this meeting
- Short-term: deploy gateway TTL tolerance (+10s) as emergency patch to staging and hold green auto-verify. (Priya + Jordan)
- Short-term: leader-election guard in route re-populate workers to prevent LRU churn (Jordan).
- Medium-term: schedule a 2-hour design session next Wed to discuss robust worker coordinator + quota refill redesign (all owners + SRE).

8) Blockers / asks
- Need SRE to allocate 1 hour tomorrow AM to run a deterministic TLS cert rotation test (owner: Tomás).
- Solutions Eng: ask for a back-compat note for customers about minor latency changes when burster pool formula changes (owner: Tomás).
- Security: review token TTL spec doc draft prior to publishing (owner: Priya).

9) Action items (who / what / due)
- Jordan: implement leader-election guard (temp) in worker loop; PR + canary by 2026-06-26 EOD.
- Priya: merge TTL tolerance patch to gateway; update logging; create Confluence spec draft; due 2026-06-27.
- Miguel: canary quota CAS tweak to shard 7 and post metrics (success/failure, refill counts) by 2026-06-26 11:00 PST.
- Tomás: pair with SRE on TLS rotation CI test and open QUIC-compat ticket; due 2026-06-27.
- All owners: be present for design session Wed 2026-07-01 10:00-12:00 (calendar invite sent).

10) Notes to self / miscellaneous fragments (informal)
- Put a short note in the sprint board: "watch for us-west-2 customer X ramp" (PLAT-ops board).
- Potential follow-up: run synthetic with mixed short/long sequences to validate new burster formula.
- Quick check: verify canary pods use runtime v1.8.3 not v1.8.2 (brief audit).

11) Retrospective quickline (what went well / bad)
- Good: small hotfix cycle for cache-ttl moved faster than expected; observability alerts triggered correctly.
- Bad: inter-service spec gaps (token TTL) created avoidable staging incidents — need stronger cross-team spec ownership.

12) Next standup focus (for next week)
- Verify leader-election guard prevents LRU churn under heavy update load.
- Measure customer-facing latency impact for burster pool formula change.
- Confirm quota refill stability across shards with new jitter.
- Finalize token TTL spec and publish to Confluence.

Appendix / logs / quick links:
- CI job: platform/controlplane/canary-run (#1973)
- Linear tickets: PLT-3421, PLT-3479, QUOTA-92, AUTH-118
- Slack: #platform-routing, #sre-cert-rotation, #auth-ops

End notes: keep this doc as the anchor for today's rotation handoff. If you add anything, put initials/date inline (e.g., "Aisha 2026-06-26: added follow-up on burster formula experiments").
